why: The wharf takes the trawlers. The deepest of them draws 4.3 m and the lowest tide of the year is 2.2 m below the mean, so a bed 7.0 m below the mean leaves 4.8 m of water at that tide: her draught and half a metre under the keel. The ground is the second issue (kept as issued in Issue2Base) with these cuts applied.
blend: Where a cut's side slope meets the old ground the two are rounded together over blendRun metres (measured along the ground, as the slope runs). Without it the slope stops at a crease, and wherever the tide's edge falls on that crease the shore is the stepped outline of the cut: the mud flat east of the basin showed it at spring low.

cuts.what: the basin off the wharf face: two trawlers lie in it, one alongside and one outside her
the way in from the open water to the south, as deep as the basin the whole way to the region's edge
the toe of the mud flat on the east bank of the way in, taken down below the lowest tide: what the channel left of it was a tongue a hand above that tide, too flat to hold a shoreline
